title: Inverse Gysin pinnings make the constant sheaf potential on a regular scheme
statement: Let $\ell$ be a prime and $\Lambda=\mathbf F_\ell$. Let $T$ be a Noetherian excellent regular scheme on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-exc-excellent-ring, def-weil-regular-scheme]; $T$ need not be connected. For $x\in T$ put $c_T(x)=\dim\mathcal O_{T,x}$, the Krull dimension of the local ring [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring], and let $i_x:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{T,x}$ be the closed-point inclusion. Use the dimension functions, twists, supported costalks $R\Gamma_x$, normalized residue transitions and pinned potential complexes of [def-per-potential-dualizing]. Then $-c_T$ is a dimension function on $T$. Let $\operatorname{Cl}_{i_x}:\Lambda(-c_T(x))[-2c_T(x)]\xrightarrow{\sim}i_x^!\Lambda=R\Gamma_x\Lambda_T$ be the absolute-purity Gysin isomorphism of the closed immersion $i_x$ of [lem-per-regular-gysin-calculus], and put $p_x=\operatorname{Cl}_{i_x}^{-1}$. These pinnings make $\Lambda_T$ a pinned potential dualizing complex for $-c_T$. For every integer $m$, the pinnings $p_x(m)[2m]$ make $\Lambda_T(m)[2m]$ a pinned potential dualizing complex for $x\mapsto m-c_T(x)$. At a generic point of $T$ the pinning of $\Lambda_T$ is the identity.
